Refugee A"Rebuild the bridge, you're saying?"
Kageaki"Yes. Timber and tools, I have a few connections for those. I will arrange them."
Kageaki"Money is not a worry you need to take on."
Refugee B"...Saying that is all very well."
Refugee A"Arre, why should WE do it? We are not the ones who broke the damn bridge!"
Kageaki"Yes."

en.html:
Kageaki"This is not rebuilding it as punishment for a wrong you did."
Refugee A"Then what is it for?"
Kageaki"Good faith."
Refugee B"...Good faith?"
Kageaki"Yes. I think you should show that you want to contribute as residents of this town, not become a burden on it."
Refugee B"..."
Refugee A"But WHY should we?! War drove us out, and somehow we managed to reach this place!"
Refugee A"We haven't done anything wrong. After all that, more hardship we must carry?! Why, bhai, WHY?"
Kageaki"...I understand how you feel. But it is also a fact that, at present, the arrival of so many people has made living conditions worse for those already here."
Refugee A"..."
Kageaki"You are not at fault. Neither are the residents."
Kageaki"If both sides plant themselves on 'I have done nothing wrong' and refuse to move, the problem also will not move. There must be some giving way on both sides."
Kageaki"And—"
Refugee B"The first ones to give way must be us."
Kageaki"...Yes."
Refugee A"...Tch... why..."
Refugee B"Don't make yourself bitter over it. Kya karein? We are the ones who came later."
Refugee B"If we want them to accept us, we have to make an effort. Put like that, it is only natural."
Refugee A"..."
Refugee B"If the residents keep looking at us like this... sooner or later, out we go. After that, we can only die by the roadside."
Refugee B"But if we manage to make peace with them—"
Kageaki"That will carry considerable weight with the authorities and the police. It will be one reason for them to favor accepting and protecting you."

ja.html:
景明「贖罪として再建するのではありません」
難民Ａ「じゃあ、何のために」
景明「誠意です」
難民Ｂ「……誠意？」
景明「はい。 　この町の厄介者になるのではなく、住民と なって貢献する意欲を示すべきと考えます」
難民Ｂ「…………」
難民Ａ「それこそ、なんでだ！ 　俺達は戦に逐われてようやくここまで辿り 着いただけなんだぞ!?」
難民Ａ「何も悪いことはしてねえ。 　なのになんで、この上そんな苦労を背負い 込まないとならないんだ……！」
景明「……お気持ちは理解できます。 　しかし、貴方がたが流入した事で、現在の ところ旧来の住民の生活環境が悪化している のも事実なのです」
難民Ａ「……」
景明「貴方がたに罪は無い。 　住民側もそれは同じ」
景明「双方が自分は悪くないと意地を張り合って いる限り、問題は解決しません。 　譲歩し合う必要があります」
景明「そして――」
難民Ｂ「先に譲歩するのは、俺達か」
景明「……はい」
難民Ａ「……ッ……なんで……」
難民Ｂ「腐るなよ。 　それは仕方ない。俺達は後から来たんだ」
難民Ｂ「受け入れて貰うために努力が必要ってのは、 当然と言えば当然の話だ」
難民Ａ「……」
難民Ｂ「このまま住民に睨まれ続ければ……いずれ 俺達は追い出される。 　そうなったら、野垂れ死にするしかない」
難民Ｂ「けれど、うまく住民側と和解できれば――」
景明「その事実は行政や警察の判断にも強く影響 するでしょう。 　受け入れ、保護する方向へ方針が傾く一因 となります」

en.html:
Refugee A"...So if we rebuild the bridge, they'll accept us?"
Kageaki"That guarantee I cannot give."
Refugee A"Very dependable, this..."
Kageaki"I am sorry. What I can promise is to work toward getting them to accept you."
Refugee A"..."
Refugee B"And the bridge-building is only us?"
Kageaki"Yes. I will help, but... I don't think we should bring in outside workers."
Kageaki"Contractors would cost money. Besides, if somebody else does the rebuilding, the whole point is lost."
Refugee B"That is true."
Refugee A"Oi... You're actually going to do it?"
Refugee B"...Yes. It's not as if my hands are occupied."
Refugee B"You also get a day's labor once a week, if that, no?"
Refugee A"..."
Refugee B"Perhaps doing it will achieve nothing. But doing nothing, we are already wasting the time. Might as well try the one that has some chance."
Refugee A"..."
Refugee A"Maybe..."
Kageaki"Then you will do it?"
Refugee B"Yes. Count me in. I'll ask the younger fellows as well."
Refugee B"But I don't think many will come... don't set your hopes too high."
Kageaki"That is quite all right. Thank you for your help."

ja.html:
難民Ａ「……あの橋を建て直せば、住民側は俺達を 認めるのか？」
景明「確約は致しかねます」
難民Ａ「あてにならねえ……」
景明「申し訳ありません。 　自分にお約束できるのは、認められるよう 働き掛ける事だけです」
難民Ａ「……」
難民Ｂ「橋造りは俺達だけで？」
景明「はい。 　自分はお手伝いしますが……外部に人手を 求めるべきではないでしょう」
景明「業者を頼むには金が掛かりますし、それに 他人の手で建て直しても意味がありません」
難民Ｂ「確かにそうだな」
難民Ａ「おい……やるつもりなのか？」
難民Ｂ「……ああ。 　どうせ体は空いてるんだ」
難民Ｂ「お前だって、日雇い仕事が週に一度あるか 無いかだろう」
難民Ａ「…………」
難民Ｂ「やっても無駄かもしれないが……やらなく たって無駄に時間を過ごすだけなんだ。 　だったら、いくらかは見込みのありそうな 方を試してみてもいい」
難民Ａ「……」
難民Ａ「かもな……」
景明「やって頂けますか」
難民Ｂ「ああ。俺は乗るよ。 　若い連中にも声を掛けてみる」
難民Ｂ「ただ、そんなには集まらないと思う……。 　あまり期待しないでくれ」
景明「結構です。 　宜しくお願いします」

Muramasa"Seems that went well."
Kageaki"For the moment."
Muramasa"But even a small river like this—putting a bridge across it is quite a job, no?"
Kageaki"I think so too. If only someone has worked as a carpenter..."
Muramasa"Am I allowed to help?"
Kageaki"...No. Not that."
Muramasa"Thought so."

en.html:
Muramasa was not a carpenter, but she could use a tsurugi's extraordinary abilities. For rebuilding a bridge, those would certainly be useful.

Very good. And how was I to explain them to the men working with me?

An ordinary policeman was not supposed to own a tsurugi. If I forced some explanation onto the matter, I might only make them suspicious and send our hard-won agreement floating away.

en.html:
After only a few minutes in the water, I understood why children did not play here. The river was not suitable for that kind of optimism.

It was deep, the bed was soft mud, and the current was fast. Given those conditions, it was no wonder that nobody had put together a temporary floating bridge, important though this crossing was.

Kageaki"Has anyone here built a bridge before?"
Refugee A"...No..."
Refugee B"...Not many people have, I imagine. Just to check, what about you?"
Kageaki"No experience. I have done construction work, but a bridge..."
Refugee A"Wah. We've barely started and already the difficulties are lined up to welcome us..."
Refugee B"...Well, the river isn't very wide. Even amateurs ought to manage something."
Kageaki"Yes. It may take some time."
Refugee A"..."
Refugee B"First let's try, na?"
Refugee A"...Fine. Complaining alone isn't going to start the work."

en.html:
Resident A"...? Oi, officer. What is today's activity? Standing in the river like that."
Resident B"Drunk again, are you?"
Kageaki"No. We are surveying the site to rebuild the bridge."
Resident B"Rebuild it? You?"
Resident B"With this lot?"
Refugee A"..."
Resident A"Hah! Good. So the police do get things done."
Resident A"Made the bridge-breakers admit it, and now they're paying for it. Very good."
Refugee A"Kya bola?!"
Refugee B"Leave it..."
Kageaki"No. That is not what is happening. These people had nothing to do with the bridge being destroyed."
Kageaki"They are not working under my orders, either. They have simply decided to rebuild it out of goodwill."
Resident A"Goodwill, is it...? Hm. If you say so."
Refugee A"..."
Resident A"Anyway, fine by me. They break it, they fix it. Why would I interfere?"
Resident A"You fellows work hard now."
Refugee A"...Tch..."
Refugee B"..."

en.html:
The two men left. Perhaps their visit had started it: the other residents nearby were now directing their attention toward us.

Not warm attention. No danger of anybody overheating from this welcome.

Naturally. Once ill feeling has settled in, it does not vacate the place so easily. For now, we could only try not to mind it. Later I would find a quiet way to say as much to the others.

en.html:
Several days went by in a flash. The work had declined to accompany them at that speed.

To speak plainly, progress was painfully slow. We were a collection of amateurs; what else could one expect? Even so, the foundations were finally beginning to take shape.
